articles: full-match-level-codes
Reject near-matching level codes before they enter a game
Security
A level-code parser can accidentally accept a prefix of malicious or malformed input if its regular expression does not match the full string.
Define a bounded grammar, normalize consistently and use full-string matching. Reject leading spaces, embedded newlines and extra suffixes unless the grammar explicitly permits them.
For the format L- followed by three digits, accept L-007 but reject L-007-extra, empty input and a thousand-character copy-paste.
Blindly stripping invalid characters may silently transform a different code into a valid one. Test exact, near-valid and oversized cases with safe error display.

content-type-and-decoder
Reject renamed HTML files masquerading as image uploads
Security
An attacker can supply an HTML payload named picture.png and forge its Content-Type. An extension and MIME header are untrusted claims.
Allowlist file extensions, inspect magic bytes and validate using an actual image decoder under bounded dimensions and memory. Re-encode when appropriate.
A claimed image/png beginning with HTML must fail before it reaches any public path. A valid PNG header with broken payload should also be rejected.
File signatures are not complete safety guarantees. Test malformed formats, polyglot inputs, decompression bombs and oversized dimensions.

csp-migration
Introduce strict Content Security Policy without breaking paid storefronts
Security
A legacy site has inline scripts and payment buttons that may fail under a newly enforced CSP, creating a business outage.
Start in report-only mode, inventory owners and inline handlers, migrate to controlled nonces or hashes, then test before enforcement. Keep a documented rollback.
An isolated trial with a nonce-based script policy reveals each blocked listener while existing checkout remains protected by the current safe policy.
Adding unsafe-inline solely to silence errors weakens XSS defenses. Test real critical flows and independent subdomains before deploying a stricter policy.

safe-player-names
Render user-supplied player names as text, never executable markup
Security
A leaderboard that writes a nickname into innerHTML can interpret tags and event handlers supplied by a player.
Use textContent for untrusted values and create trusted elements through DOM APIs. Validate length and display normalization before storing any nickname.
A name containing must appear literally as text, not create an image or attempt script execution after reload.
Client-side validation can be bypassed by directly calling a server endpoint. Verify server-side constraints and all later rendering contexts.

local-progress-trust
Distinguish local progress convenience from real purchase entitlement
Security
Browser localStorage is writable by the user and may be cleared automatically in private browsing. It is suitable for game progress but not for charging customers.
Validate persisted objects, clamp unlocked stages to documented bounds and catch storage exceptions. Keep paid downloads behind independent server-side authorization.
If a stored level changes from 8 to 999999, the game must clamp or reset safely. Editing a flag must not unlock a paid file.
A browser-side 'paid=true' value is never reliable proof of payment. Test spoofed storage, quota failures and browser data clearing.

atomic-versioned-publish
Avoid partial customer-facing releases during bulk uploads
Security
Publishing an HTML page before its linked scripts and assets creates a broken public interval and makes rollback uncertain.
Upload complete files to private same-filesystem staging, validate owner and file hashes, then atomically rename into a previously absent versioned public directory.
With release R1, users see either no R1 or the complete R1 directory; never publish R1 index while its game file is still being copied.
Directory rename is not atomic across filesystems, and shared hosts require symlink checks. Simulate interruption halfway through staging.

rollback-sha-verification
Prevent old deployment rollback from overwriting new improvements
Security
After deployment A completes, another authorized workflow might change the same file. A blind rollback from A would destroy newer work.
Save the exact pre- and post-install SHA-256 values and only restore while current bytes still match A's deployed digest.
If A wrote hash X and B subsequently wrote hash Y, A must refuse a rollback rather than replacing B's version with its old snapshot.
Timestamps alone cannot prove file identity. Test competing changes and require a clear mismatch error without mutation.

public-manifest-evidence
Prove a publicly served game matches its release manifest
Security
A green workflow is not evidence that visitors see the correct bytes; caching or a wrong document root can serve old files.
Include release ID, expected paths, digest values and commit SHA in a manifest. Verify each public URL externally and test interactive behavior in Chrome.
Compare the served game's SHA against its release record and confirm a browser test marker appears in the rendered result.
Checking only repository contents can miss a blocked cPanel transfer. Maintain per-file results with HTTP status and browser evidence.

cache-release-boundaries
Prevent mixed HTML and JavaScript versions after a site update
Security
Old cached JavaScript combined with fresh HTML can create broken game states and impossible reproduction steps.
Use immutable versioned asset filenames and a controlled entry HTML refresh strategy. Bind application state schema to explicit release versions.
When logic changes, publish app.abcd1234.js and let the new index reference that filename; do not silently replace a shared cached file.
Aggressive service-worker caching can pin old HTML indefinitely. Test warm and cold clients and service-worker activation logic.

paid-delivery-boundary
Keep free play previews separate from purchase authorization
Security
A free browser-game preview and a paid download might share a page, tempting developers to gate downloads with JavaScript booleans.
Let previews run publicly, but require payment verification, order ownership and server-side entitlement before sending a purchased file.
Editing localStorage from paid=false to paid=true must not let a visitor download an order they did not purchase.
A success animation after sending a wallet transaction is not verified settlement. Test replay attacks, failed purchases and refunded orders in a nonproduction environment.
